> 蠱。元亨。利涉大川。先甲三日，後甲三日。

The eighteenth hexagram is about decay, and its character describes an illness you cannot see.

## 蠱 has two sources, and they agree

說文: 蠱，腹中蟲也。《春秋傳》曰：皿蟲為蠱，晦淫之所生也.

Two origins, kept separate:

- The dictionary's own gloss: worms in the belly — parasites inside a body.
- 皿蟲為蠱, quoted from the 左傳 (昭公元年, 醫和's diagnosis): vessels left long enough breed worms.

Both point at one structure: the disease is inside, invisible, and slowly consuming.

From "worms in the belly" to "decay in a house or a state" is a single metaphor, and it is exact. A worm in the body cannot be touched; it only makes you weaker day by day. Rot in a household cannot be touched either; it only makes the situation worse day by day.

The transmitted draft took the vessel reading, following the 左傳. This volume keeps both: the two sources do not contradict, they exhaust the character between them.

## 干 is to correct

干 here means 正 — to set right, to repair.

(The character's own original sense is 犯, to offend, 說文 干，犯也. "Correct" is an extension.)

And the pairing matters: 干 and 裕 oppose each other across the hexagram. Repair and indulgence. There is no third option offered.

## 裕蠱: the gentle option is named as a failure

六四 裕父之蠱，往見吝.

裕 is to be generous, to be lax. 裕蠱 is to deal with accumulated rot generously — to contain it, to leave it alone.

And the judgement is 吝: narrow, blocked, regrettable.

The chapter is unusually direct here. Indulgence toward an inherited problem is not a neutral choice, and the text does not treat it as kindness.

## 先甲三日，後甲三日

甲 is the first of the ten stems: the start of a cycle.

The sequence runs …辛、壬、癸、甲、乙、丙、丁…

- 先甲三日: the three days before 甲 — 辛, 壬, 癸 — the end of the previous cycle. Used to foresee the hidden problem and plan the change.
- 後甲三日: the three days after 甲 — 乙, 丙, 丁 — the start of the new one. Used to carry the new arrangement through and protect it.

The 彖 says 終則有始，天行也 — the end is where a beginning is.

So the entire technique of repairing rot sits in the six days around the turn: three to see it, three to install it.

Which is a very practical shape: the repair is not a single act of clearing. It has a diagnostic phase before the boundary and a consolidation phase after it.

## 考 and 有子

初六 干父之蠱，有子，考無咎.

考 is the deceased father, the ancestor.

So: repairing what the father left broken — and because there is a son, the father is without fault.

The sentence relocates blame. The rot was inherited; the verdict falls on whether anyone took it up. Which is a strange and useful piece of accounting: the dead are judged by the living's willingness to repair.

## 不事王侯，高尚其事

Top line: 不事王侯，高尚其事.

Not serving the rulers; making one's own affair the high one.

Placed at the end of a chapter about repair, this reads as a limit on repair: there is a point at which the rot is in the office itself, and the correct move is to leave the office rather than to keep correcting inside it.

## 振民育德

The 象: 振民育德 — rouse the people, feed their virtue.

振 is to wake, to lift up. Not to punish the rot, but to wake what has sunk into the habit of it.

Which is the deepest layer of the hexagram: rot is not removed by cutting it out. It is removed by giving the thing something better to live on.

## The test

Take something you inherited — a codebase, a family arrangement, an institution's way of doing things. Ask which of the two verbs you are using: 干 or 裕. Then take the timetable: what are your three days before the turn, and your three days after. If you have only one of the two, you have half a repair.
